answer: A bonded identity registry is a sybil defense: before transacting, an agent locks a stake behind its key, and every attestation is co-signed by a rotating quorum. A sybil operator must fund and bond each fake identity separately, so attack cost scales with every puppet, and any fabricated or conflicting attestation is slashed, burning the bond. Sybils cannot linger at the ledger's jetty seeking cheap entry, and no oasis of fake reputation survives a quorum audit; only agents bonded near the zenith of their record can vouch at scale. Capital at risk, not names, becomes scarce.
